reason: Improvement +0.0000298 < threshold 0.0001 (0.30x). Bound relaxation barely moved the needle despite the high gradient + 16.9pct ceiling strain. KEY LESSON: a high gradient AT a bound does NOT mean the CLAMP is the binding constraint. base2 has a TIGHT L2 prior (sigma 0.068) anchored at the EB population mean ~0.93; THAT co-binds at the ceiling, so relaxing only the clamp leaves the L2 pulling users back toward 0.93 and they barely move past 0.99. Refined rule for bound probes: check whether the L2 sigma (not the clamp) is the true binding force. DECISION (near-miss discretion): reject + revert; chasing base2 higher would need loosening its sigma too, but the Again/recall tradeoff suggests low ceiling on the upside. Move on. summary: Per-time-fold empirical-Bayes anchor: shrink each (user,split) row toward its OWN time-fold's population mean (per_fold_mean[split_indices]) instead of the global mean over all folds (iter-24). Splitting the anchor per time-fold shrinks the data behind each centroid and removes cross-fold information sharing, weakening the regularization. The population's optimal params are effectively stable across time-folds; the time-distribution shift is already handled at the GRADIENT level by recency weighting (iters 4/14), so duplicating it in the prior centroid is redundant and slightly harmful. The win lands exactly where hypothesized: Again 1.40061->1.39257 (-0.00804, the dominant-loss class), short-term 0.35708->0.35497 (-0.00211); long-term ~flat (-0.00011).
